summary: CFD vs. Reality: The Accuracy Debate

scenes.title: CFD vs. Reality: The Accuracy Debate
scenes.narration: CFD simulations use numerical methods to predict fluid behavior, while real-world experiments provide empirical data. The key question is how closely these two approaches align, often revealing differences.

scenes.title: Modeling vs. Measuring
scenes.narration: CFD builds a digital model of fluid dynamics, solving equations to predict flow. Experiments directly measure physical phenomena, capturing real-world complexities and providing ground truth.

scenes.title: Factors Influencing Accuracy
scenes.narration: CFD accuracy depends on the mesh resolution, the fidelity of physical models like turbulence, and precise input data. Each factor introduces potential errors.

scenes.title: Aerospace Wing Design
scenes.narration: In aerospace, CFD simulates airflow over a wing, predicting lift and drag. These predictions are then rigorously compared against wind tunnel experiments for validation, often showing 5-10% differences.

scenes.title: Complementary Tools for Innovation
scenes.narration: CFD and experiments are complementary tools, not replacements. CFD accelerates design iteration and explores scenarios, while experiments provide critical validation, leading to robust engineering solutions.
